text_fidelity_a:
Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+ I ADORE the idea of this kit! It is seriously awesome! There's no clean up whatsoever, so my little ones can "paint" and learn to their heart's content, and I don't have to worry about them staining clothes or painting the walls. If it was designed a bit sturdier, it would be an amazing "busy bag" item(without supervision).

When these cards first came in the mail, I saw that there was a white sticker(of sorts) over the card. Getting this sticker wet makes the picture show up. I knew without supervision, that sticker could be torn up quickly or logged with water. I sat with my boys as they took turns "painting" the cards. They were gentle! Still, as the sticker dried, I saw more and more scratches showing up, which means the picture underneath is no longer hidden(though you can still pretty much see what it's going to be anyway...the white sticker doesn't hide it 100% even with no scratches) I was disappointed that it ended up being so fragile.

I recommend letting your little one have a large space, so that he/she doesn't have to stack the cards together as they dry. We were on the porch the first time my boys used them, and I lay them individually on the porch rail. I stacked them when we came in the house, though. I'm sure that is part of the scratching problem. Unfortunately, that leaves out the places that this kit would come in most handy, like car rides, doctor waiting rooms, and church(for especially young ones). It also makes the key ring that is included pretty worthless.

The little brush is two pieces. You simply unscrew the top, fill it with water, and then put it back together. It worked well, and we didn't have issue with leaking.

Overall, once again, I absolutely adore the idea of this kit, but I wish the cards weren't so fragile.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+

Stay away.

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Grow Your Own Crystal Mini Worlds Craft and Science Kit The "Grow your own Crystal Mini Worlds" kit is a good one. It is a bit complicated compared to other craft kits of it's ilk, and requires a good amount of time, planning, and careful activation and storage of the key components, as you'll use things from project to project.

The crafts themselves are pretty impressive as well. The crystals all grew for me, which is often something that we struggle with in our home with other crystal growing kits, and the number of differnt ways your children can put them together is quite impressive. There is some modeling clay that can help with creating unique items, and there are a number of different design elements as well.

The biggest drawbacks are twofold - this requires older children, and it will definitely require more adult supervision and planning than your average arts and crafts kit, not only in terms of handling the heating, but also in aiding in the planning and reading stages of craft creation. Additionally, while I've become used to having crafting materials stored all around my home, this one takes the cake in terms of storing solutions, setting up crystal growing areas that cannot be disturbed, drying areas, and set up areas that will take over your crafting area (or in my case, the dining room) for multiple nights to multiple weeks if you make your way through projects quickly.

Cherry-O Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive) You really can't go wrong with this game if you've got little ones around(unless, of course, they put things other than food in their mouth, and then I'd save this for later). It's a classic board game for a reason.

My husband has fond memories of playing this game with his grandmother, but about a month ago was the first time I'd ever played it. My children have fallen in love with the game, and I'm thrilled they've had the chance to experience it. It's cute and fun!

It's a really quick and simple game to play, and easy enough for very young players to be included, since counting only goes to 4 in the game. (Again, the fruit is very small, though, so don't have it around those that put things in their mouths.) It's actually just right for my 3 year old, and while it's technically too easy for my 5 and 8 year old children, they still love playing it.

Also, with small pieces, I appreciate that there are 4 extra pieces of fruit(one of each color) included in case one goes missing.

Overall, this is a perfect game for preschoolers to play, as long as they don't put things in their mouth.

text_fidelity_a:
Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands

Bezier Games One Week Ultimate Werewolf "Werewolf" games from Bezier games are becoming a bit ubiquitous at this point. That said, the core gameplay of the original, and certain spinoff titles like Inquisition have worked well for me in the past. "One Night" never really floated my boat, as it was too short and chaotic, so the "One Week" version seemed like a good fit.

In this game, you're moving around a castle board searching for Werewolves. You can do many "One Night" things - switch tokens without knowing who you are or who you become, and you need to bluff about which cards you are using. Unfortunately, this game shares a little too much from many of the same flaws that I noticed with One Night Ultimate Werewolf - it's too chaotic, it's still too quick, and you still will struggle to make strategic decisions because you don't often know what you are doing when you take actions. For people who enjoy the strategy-less designer games, like Talisman or traditional Werewolf, then this might be a hit if you have the right group.

For the right group, this will be a big success. While I do like it more than "One Night", it's not quite ready for my tastes yet.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games One Week Ultimate Werewolf

LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil The letters in this book aren't done in order. If you're wanting this book to teach letters, that might be important to know. I've chosen to teach in order, and am working on that with my two oldest. (I know some teach letters out of order, which is great, too) Either way, with this book they're learning letters. Plus, there's an alphabet chart on the last page that does put the letters in the correct order. It seems as though the letters in this book are introduced according to how easy they are to write(straight lines, curves, etc). So, as your child goes along, the letters get harder and harder to write.

Also, both uppercase and lowercase letters are included in this book.

Each page in the book has a little practice sheet. These sheets are super sensitive to pressure. Any pressure at all from any source, and a "pencil" mark will show up where you've written. Once you've used these sheets, they are useless. (You can't erase) You are provided with an extra set of sheets, and given the warning to NOT stack and to separate them before writing. When your little one is done with the sheets, they can be easily torn out, and the book will work perfectly fine without them. Your child can still practice "writing" letters just using the book.

Since music is an important part of this book's story, I enjoyed that added lesson for my little ones. There's even a piano included that can be played, which makes me like this book even more.

Overall, this is a wonderful tool to have for learning! I'm looking forward to adding the numbers book to our library soon!
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil

LEGO The Movie 2 Pop-Up Party Bus 70828 Building Kit, Build Your Own Toy Party Bus for 9+ Year Old Girls and Boys (1013 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I like this set much more than my daughter does. This set is over 1,000 pieces, making it a very difficult build for younger players, but it does have a lot of individual elements that make up this particular set. There are multiple levels within the vehicle, elements that unfold or open up, and each is constructed separately. Ultimately, you'll feel good about the fact that you've done it, but both of us have to admit that the end result is less impressive than some of the other sets that we've built together recently. This is compact, and not outwardly "cool" as it's really just an awkwardly shaped bus that could double as a spaceship. The characters are in line with the "Friends" series, so they definitely look like they don't belong with many of the basic sets. There is some play value here, but once you play with the folding and unfolding, there's less here than it appears.

Overall, if you're a fan of the movies, this may be an essential item. For us, it was a challenging pass.

text_fidelity_a:
Arcade Claw Game: Maker Lab (Klutz STEM Kit) Brown/a, 9.8" x 2.5" x 11.8" The promise of this kit is that it's difficult. The final product, if it works according to specifications, looks amazing, and should teach some important concepts in a fun and interesting way. And this kit does accomplish a lot of what it sets out to do - it's hard to build, requires a little dexterity, and does work reasonably well after construction is complete - all while being a fun teaching tool.

This kit is labeled for use with smaller kids, but realistically a child will need to be around age nine or so to build this with minimal assistance from an adult. There are many steps, and it requires the ability to tie knots, balance pieces, and do some basic measurement.

Perhaps the strongest element of this kit is the booklet - steps are clear and easy to follow, although there are quite a few of them before a finished product is complete - and it does have a brief introduction that teaches the concepts of pulleys.

The downside of this kit is that, yes, it's difficult and time consuming. Unless your kid is an engineer in the making, it will require parental assistance. It's easy to quit, and if you do decide to leave it in the middle, it can be difficult to pick up where you left off. That said, difficulty is something that a lot of us want, so if you know it going in, then it's no big deal. The final product promises a lot, and surprisingly, it delivers, but the plastic side panels that hold the kit together are a bit flimsy, and require extra support.

Overall, we're impressed.
text_fidelity_b: Arcade Claw Game: Maker Lab (Klutz STEM Kit) Brown/a, 9.8" x 2.5" x 11.8"

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:58af1484fac2632df11b3d8e403acedc]] Addendum: Two years old now and these toys are still working great and popular with the kids. I assume the ease of filling in the pool and the ability to shoot whatever they want without getting fussed at adds to their appeal.

I got both the Matchbox Aqua Cannon Swamp Blaster and this Fire Truck Rig for 5 and 6 year old grandkids. Until I showed them how to use the toys, they didn't show much interest in them. Once the trucks were filled and squirting, however, they happily shot at their sister for about 15 minutes. It didn't keep their interest long but there were enough kids to share the toys that they stayed in action for an hour or so.

They toys fill easily and are easy to load and shoot. We submerged the trucks in the pool so that they self-filled meaning that only the kids were only limited by their ability to keep pumping (see photo).

I find these a great alternative to water guns. The volume and strength of the shots are less than those oversized guns but enough to shoot all the way across the pool. Because they are not guns, the kids are less likely to feel the need to aim them at people.

I think these toys are best suited for ages five and under.

1 year followup: This toy spent the winter outside by the pool and it still works like new. I have to keep it out of the hands of adults who delight in shooting water far outside the pool area (violating house rules).
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

Barbie Printastic Hair Doll Barbie Hair Tattoos Doll has fast become a favorite doll in our household. The girls in our family have always loved styling Barbie doll's hair as much as they love coordinating her wardrobe and styling her home. The doll itself is simply beautiful with her hip length blonde hair, mod print mini dress and high heels.

Barbie also comes with a styling salon chair, 13 tattoo design strips, a flat iron, comb, hair clip, 2 hair bands, 3 barrettes and a water bottle. To make Barbie's hair decorated with the colorful tattoo designs, you comb out her hair smooth, clip one of the 13 tattoo designs to her hair, spray it with water and then swipe it with the flat iron. The tattoo ink is non staining- thank goodness, as sometimes they get left on a table after using.

We quickly found that experimenting with the hair amount and smoothness, the water being cold, warm or hot and the pressure and speed we use with the flat iron do affect the way the tattoos come out on Barbie's hair. We also noticed that some tattoos come out way better than others, no matter what you do. We found that really flat combed hair, warm water and pulling the flat iron hard and slowly gave some great results on some of the tattoo patterns. Others just looked like color blobs.

This all really didn't even seem to matter, as the girls love this doll and especially when the tattoos came out looking pretty good in her hair. When they didn't look good, the tattoos just washed out in a minute. For the tattoos that didn't turn out on Barbie, the girls ended up putting the tattoos on themselves as bracelets on their wrists or ankles. They had fun no matter if the tattoos came out good or bad looking in Barbie's hair, so this Barbie Hair Tattoos is still worth 4 Stars, even though you have to experiment to get some of the tattoos to look great.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Printastic Hair Doll

Barbie Dream House Arrived yesterday in a big box. Parts loosely tossed inside, some in plastic bags. The included instructions are so BAD that we didn't/couldn't even use them to assemble the Dream House. We relied mainly on the pictures on the front of the box to guide us.

Pieces are initially hard to snap together. Some of the white columns go in very specific places so I had to take some out and replace them with others. Luckily, I had 2 kids and another adult helping me assemble this thing. The main elevator gets stuck at the second level and I need to work on that some more to get it functioning properly, if possible. The plastic parts are durable enough, I still felt I had to be extra careful to avoid breaking any of them. After we had it mostly assembled I was able to finally snap all the columns in place whereas before no matter how hard I tried I couldn't get them to snap firmly into the bases.

A LOT of accessories are included from silverware to bathroom fixtures, jewelry, etc...so there are LOT of small parts to suck up in the vacuum cleaner or for a pet (like ours) to chew up. We will have to be extra careful about those but they are nice to have to complete the Dream House environment. A sticker page is included that you peel and stick to various areas of the house to make it seem more realistic - fireplace, etc...

Although I had a hard time assembling it (don't try to assemble it on an empty stomach), I didn't for once lose my cool and toss it out the window. We got it assembled, it looks pretty cool to be honest. And my 9 year old daughter absolutely went nuts over it. She loves Barbie and this Dream House is like a parallel Universe to her which she can escape into make-believe land instead of watching TV. Even her tomboy sister likes to play with it. I don't know if it will maintain it's appeal after a while, but despite it's difficulty in assembly, and the horrible instructions (just small black and white pictures, no words whatsoever), you can assemble it if you are patient and keep trying different parts and studying the pictures on the box.

And it's pretty tall....at least 4 feet high. The barbie dolls fit nicely inside of it and overall it's a pretty cool thing to look at when it's completely assembled and all the furniture and stuff is placed inside it. I would have loved to have had one of these when I was a kid. Is it worth $159.00? I don't know. I might would have paid at least a hundred for it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream House
